h1:
Dream World Pathum Thani
A Full Day at the Khlong Sam Theme Park
intro: Dream World is the theme park that most Bangkok and suburban families grew up with. It sits along Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok Road on the Khlong Sam side of Pathum Thani, less than an hour's drive from Bangkok. In one place you get white-knuckle rides, gentle rides for small kids, pretty garden photo spots, and a real sub-zero snow room. We've pulled together everything you need to know before you go — the standout rides, ticket prices, and how to get there — all in one spot.

blocks.html: Dream World has been open since 1993 and is a large theme park spread across more than 160 rai (about 25 hectares) in Bueng Yi Tho, along Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok Road at KM 7 on the Khlong Sam side. The big draw is that you can spend the whole day in one place, with the park divided into several zones such as Dream Garden (a photo-friendly garden), Fantasy Land (a fairy-tale zone for kids), and Adventure Land (the thrill rides). It works well for families with both small children and teenagers going together.
Dream World has more than 40 rides, from gentle ones built for photos to stomach-dropping thrill machines. We've picked the ones people talk about most so you can plan what to ride first.

items.name: Sky Coaster
items.blurb: The looping roller coaster that's been Dream World's signature for years. It climbs high, then plunges and rolls through a loop. A must for thrill seekers. The line gets long in the afternoon, so ride it in the morning.

items.name: Hurricane
items.blurb: Another hard-hitting coaster with tight, sharp turns one after another. If you love speed and G-forces, don't skip it. It keeps you on edge from the moment it launches.

items.name: Viking
items.blurb: A big Viking ship that swings back and forth until it's nearly vertical. The moment you lift off the seat is the highlight. It's a ride the whole family can do, as long as you can handle a bit of a thrill.

items.name: Tornado
items.blurb: Spinning seats that whirl and flip on several axes at once. Dizzying but fun, and a good next step if you've already done Viking and want to crank up the intensity.

items.name: Grand Canyon (rapids ride)
items.blurb: A simulated whitewater rafting ride in a round boat that drifts through waterfalls and rapids — you will get soaked. Perfect on a hot day. Bring a spare shirt or a rain poncho.

items.name: Super Splash
items.blurb: A boat that slides down a tall drop and smacks into the water, throwing spray over the whole boat. Soaking-wet fun. People in the queue can watch the splash from the spot down below.

items.name: Bumper Boat / Bumper Car
items.blurb: Bumper cars and bumper boats for gentle crashes that kids love. It's something the whole family can hop on together without any of the scares.

items.name: Fantasy Land kids' rides
items.blurb: A carousel, a mini train, spinning teacups, and other gentle rides for small children who aren't ready for the big stuff yet. There's a fairy-tale castle zone for photos too.

blocks.title: Plan your ride order to make it count
blocks.html: Thrill rides like Sky Coaster and Hurricane have the longest lines in the afternoon. If you buy an all-ride ticket, head straight for the popular ones in the morning, then save the kids' zone and photo spots for the cooler, shadier part of the afternoon.

blocks.html: Snow Town is the highlight that many people come specifically to experience. It's a real snow room kept at around -5°C, with snow inside to mold and play with, an ice slide to glide down, and winter-themed photo spots. It's great for kids and for anyone who wants to feel snow without flying abroad.

items: Charged separately — the snow zone costs around an extra 190 THB per person and isn't included in the standard ride ticket.
Cold-weather gear provided — the park lends out winter coats and boots, but it's worth wearing your own thick socks and long pants too.
Limited time per session — you can usually stay inside for about 30–40 minutes per session, plenty for photos and a few goes on the slide.
Watch very small children — the sub-zero air can be too cold for little ones; if they start shivering, take them out early.

blocks.html: Dream World sells tickets in packages so you can pick based on how much you want to ride. The prices below are rough ranges for Thai visitors and can change with promotions and holiday periods. Always check dreamworld.co.th or call 0-2577-8666 before you go.

items.name: Admission only
items.blurb: Enter the park, walk around for photos, and watch the shows, but rides aren't included. Starts around 250 THB per person. Best for people who mainly want to stroll and take pictures.

items.name: All-ride ticket (one go each)
items.blurb: Admission plus the 26 rides in the package, one ride each. Around 500 THB per person. Good value for families who don't plan to repeat rides.

items.name: All-ride ticket (unlimited repeats)
items.blurb: Admission plus unlimited rides on the package all day. Around 600 THB per person. The best value if you plan to ride the popular ones several times.

blocks.title: Ticket details worth knowing
blocks.html: All-ride tickets usually don't include the snow zone and a few special rides, which you pay for on site. Children under the height limit and seniors often get special prices, so bring an ID card in case you need to confirm eligibility.

items: The Grand Canyon backdrop — a large canyon-style rock set that gives photos a faraway feel. It's one of the most-photographed corners in the park.
Dream Garden — flower beds and fountains decorated in bright colors, with a long stretch to walk and shoot. Morning and late-afternoon light looks better than midday.
The Fantasy Land castle — a pastel fairy-tale castle that makes for cute photos with the kids.
Inside Snow Town — all-white snow scenes and winter decor that look like a real trip to a cold country.

blocks.text: Making the most of a family day out

blocks.html: Dream World suits families because the rides are clearly split by age. Small kids stick to Fantasy Land, teens head for Sky Coaster, and adults who skip the thrill rides can walk around taking photos and sit down for the shows. Here's a rough plan to follow.

blocks.label: Morning half
blocks.title: Knock out the popular rides before the crowds

items.activity: Arrive at the park, buy an all-ride ticket, and head straight for the big rides after you're through the gate
items.note: Coming early avoids the midday heat and long lines

items.activity: Ride Sky Coaster and Hurricane while the lines are still short
items.note: Check the height limit before you queue

items.activity: Do the Grand Canyon rapids ride and Super Splash
items.note: You'll get soaked, so have a spare shirt ready

items.activity: Break for lunch inside the park
items.note: Restaurants inside cost a little more than outside

items.activity: Take the little ones to Fantasy Land for the carousel and bumper cars
items.note: The sun has eased off by now, so it's comfortable to walk

items.activity: Head into Snow Town (pay on site)
items.note: Grab the cold-weather gear before going in; you can stay about 30–40 minutes

items.activity: Get your photos at the Grand Canyon and Dream Garden
Catch the closing show, then stop by the gift shop before heading home
items.note: Check the show times on the board by the entrance

blocks.html: Dream World is at 62 Moo 1, Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok Road KM 7, Bueng Yi Tho, Thanyaburi District, Pathum Thani (the Khlong Sam area). From Bangkok it's about a 45-minute to one-hour drive depending on traffic.

items: Private car — take Vibhavadi or Phahonyothin Road toward Rangsit, turn onto Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok Road, and drive straight to KM 7. There's a large parking lot at the park.
SRT Red Line train — ride to Rangsit station (the terminus), then take a taxi or hired ride about 7 km along Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok Road. A good way to dodge the morning traffic.
Vans / songthaews — from Future Park Rangsit or Rangsit Market, vans and songthaews run the Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok route and pass in front of Dream World. Tell the driver to drop you at the park.
Public bus — route 538 and joint-service buses run the Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok route past the entrance. Ask the driver before boarding whether it passes Dream World.

blocks.title: Which day to go
blocks.html: Weekdays are far quieter than weekends and long holidays, with barely any lines for the rides. If you can choose, go on a weekday, and check the opening and closing times for the day on the website first, since on some low-season days the park closes earlier than usual.

faq.q: How much does Dream World cost to enter?
faq.a: Rough prices: admission only starts around 250 THB, an all-ride ticket (one go each) is about 500 THB, and an unlimited all-day all-ride ticket is about 600 THB. The Snow Town snow zone costs around an extra 190 THB. Prices can change with promotions, so check dreamworld.co.th before you go.

faq.q: How cold is the Dream World snow zone, and what should I bring?
faq.a: Snow Town is kept at around -5°C. The park lends out winter coats and boots, but you should wear your own thick socks and long pants too. Keep an eye on very small children — if they start shivering, take them out early.

faq.q: Can small children enjoy Dream World?
faq.a: Easily. Fantasy Land has gentle rides for little ones such as the carousel, spinning teacups, bumper cars, and a mini train, plus a fairy-tale castle for photos. The thrill rides have height limits posted.

faq.q: Can I get to Dream World by the SRT Red Line?
faq.a: Yes. Take the Red Line to Rangsit station, which is the terminus, then take a taxi or hired ride about 7 km along Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok Road. It's a good option for avoiding the morning traffic.

faq.q: Which day is best to visit Dream World?
faq.a: Weekdays are far quieter than weekends and long holidays, with barely any lines for the rides. Come in the morning to ride the popular ones before the queues build, and check each day's opening and closing times before you travel.
